findings.problem: Caption 2, 'Short rounds leave more trail, so more ants follow.' (3.4-6.2 s), runs ahead of its picture. 'More ants follow' is shown by the ten ant dots turning orange, but for the first 1.6 s of the caption almost none are orange: one dot at rounds 1 and 2, then ZERO at round 3 (4.5-5.0 s, the real count is onBest = 1, 1, 0, 4, 5, 4, 6, 6, 9, 10), and only at round 4 (5.0 s) do four dots light up. So during 4.5-5.0 s the caption states the opposite of what the dots show.
findings.fix: Split the claim to match the picture: caption 2a [3.4, 4.9] 'Short rounds leave more trail.' (trails are visibly thickening) and 2b [5.1, 6.4] 'So more ants follow it.' (4-5 dots orange from 5.0 s); keep caption 3 at 6.5 s. Alternatively start the caption at about 5.0 s.
findings.evidence: Stills s8@3.6 (caption on, 1 orange dot), s8@4.5 (round 3, no orange dot, caption still 'so more ants follow'), s8@5.3 (round 4, 4 dots). The time-lapse maps round = floor(14 * ramp(t, 3.1, 10.8) + 0.5), so round 3 shows 4.475-5.025 s. Dot counts from L8.SNOW.hist[r].onBest, which matches the lesson's own colony run.

findings.problem: The word 'round' means two different things on the same screen. The tags 'round 3' (scene 8), 'round 1/2' (scene 2) and '40 runs, 20 rounds each' (scene 9) mean one pass of the loop, but 'trail on best round', 'best round' and 'stuck on a poor round' (scenes 8 and 9) and the captions 'Short rounds leave more trail' and 'settles on one short round' mean one tour (a round trip). The lessons, bank and boss use the opposite split: 'iteration' for a pass of the loop (the 8.1 demo says 'Run 1 iteration', 'Iteration') and 'round' for a tour ('best round so far', 'shortest round is 114.5 km'). A learner will read 'best round' as 'the best of the rounds, e.g. round 2', and will meet 'iteration' in the app and the quiz.
findings.fix: Say 'iteration' for the loop pass (tags 'iteration 3', header '40 runs, 20 iterations each', scene 2 'iteration 1/2') and keep 'round' only for a tour, as the lessons do; or call a tour a 'tour' everywhere ('trail on best tour', 'best 115.1 km tour').
findings.evidence: Stills s8@4.5 ('round 3' beside 'trail on best round' and 'best 115.1 km'), s9@12.3 ('20 rounds each' beside 'trail on the best round' / 'stuck on a poor round'). grep of videos/l8/scene-*.js finds no 'iteration' at all; js/content/nic/l8-01.js and js/bank/nic-46.js use iteration for the pass and round for the tour.

findings.problem: The video never uses the lessons' technical words: 'pheromone', 'heuristic' (eta), tau and eta, 'iteration'. It says 'trail' and 'closeness' instead, and nothing says trail = pheromone or closeness = heuristic. 'closeness' is not in the lessons, bank or boss quiz at all. A first-time learner who watches the video and then meets 'pheromone' and 'heuristic' in the lesson, Revise and the boss will not connect them. The storyboard colour note says 'blue = pheromone (tau)' and 'purple = closeness (eta)', but none of that is on screen.
findings.fix: Add one bridge on screen the first time each term appears: scene 2 legend tag 'trail (pheromone)' (or a second small tag), and scene 4 header 'closeness (heuristic)'. That is enough; keep the friendly words afterwards. Optionally show tau and eta as tiny labels in scene 4.
findings.evidence: grep -i 'pheromone|heuristic|iteration' over videos/l8/scene-*.js only hits a code comment. Lessons: l8-02.js 'The rule mixes pheromone tau (learned) with a heuristic eta (fixed)'; the 'Which ingredient does the colony update' check; boss and bank use pheromone throughout.

findings.problem: The rows are labelled 'Elitist rank' and 'Max-Min', and the red bars say that 'Max-Min' leaves 17 of 40 runs stuck. But the simulation behind the bars is 'best ant only deposits' with no trail limits. Lesson 8.4 says the defining feature of Max-Min is that it keeps every trail between a minimum and a maximum so a road never becomes certain, which is exactly the anti-stagnation device. The lesson therefore names this row 'Best ant only (Max-Min style)' and the bank says 'Max-Min style: only the best ant'. The video drops 'style', so a learner leaves believing the real Max-Min Ant System is the one most likely to get stuck.
findings.fix: Relabel row 3 'Max-Min style · best 1' (and row 2 'Elitist rank · best 3' is acceptable as the lesson names it). Or add a small grey note under the bars, 'simple versions: no trail limits'. Do not change the numbers.
findings.evidence: videos/l8/scene-09-variants.js NAMES = ['Ant System · all', 'Elitist rank · best 3', 'Max-Min · best 1']; js/content/nic/l8-03.js MODES 'Best ant only (Max-Min style)' and the 'Who deposits?' step ('Max-Min also keeps every trail between a minimum and a maximum'); js/bank/nic-47.js line 92. Still s9@12.3 shows 'Max-Min · best 1' with '17 of 40'.

findings.problem: 'stuck on a poor round: over 116 km' overstates the data. The shortest possible round is 114.5 km (the scene itself asserts that 116 'sits just above the shortest round'), and the shortest is never shown on screen, so a learner cannot tell that 'poor' means 1.7% to 7.5% above the best. In the 40 runs, the counted colonies end at 116.4 to 123.1 km (all ants: 116.4, 117.6, 119.1; best 1: 116.4 x5 up to 123.1). 'Stuck' is not measured either: the test is only that the best tour after 20 iterations is over 116 km.
findings.fix: Show the yardstick and soften the wording: add a small grey tag 'shortest possible: 114.5 km' under the header and rename the red legend 'missed the best: over 116 km' (or 'ended above 116 km'); caption 4 'But more runs miss the best round.' Keep 3 / 5 / 17 of 40.
findings.evidence: Node run of L8.colony seeds 1-40, beta 1, 20 iterations: stuck tour lengths 116.4 to 123.1 km; L8.TEN.opt = 114.478. Still s9@12.3 (legend 'stuck on a poor round: over 116 km', no optimum shown). Assert in scene-09: L8.same(L8.TEN.opt < POOR && POOR - L8.TEN.opt < 2, true, ...).

findings.problem: The captions give one dial the credit for a result that needs both. 'Alpha 0: trails ignored, the nearest wins' (82%) is produced by alpha 0 AND beta 3 (the beta knob also slides 1 to 3 at the same moment); 'Beta 0: only trails count, the strongest wins' (74%) needs alpha 3. With only alpha set to 0 (beta still 1) Kell gets 43%; with only beta set to 0 (alpha still 1) Sowe gets 43%. 'wins' also overclaims: Kell takes 82% of the choices, not all. The mode tag reads 'alpha = 0: trails ignored' and does not show that beta is now 3.
findings.fix: Say both settings: caption 3 'Alpha 0, beta 3: trails ignored, the nearest is favoured.' and caption 4 'Beta 0, alpha 3: only trails count, the strongest is favoured.' and make the mode tags 'α = 0, β = 3: trails ignored' / 'α = 3, β = 0: closeness ignored'. Or move only one dial at a time (alpha to 0 with beta kept at 3 from the start).
findings.evidence: Stills s6@7.6 (dials 0 and 3, caption 'Alpha 0: ... the nearest wins') and s6@10.8 (dials 3 and 0). Node check of the courier rule: (alpha 0, beta 1) = 43/21/17/11/9 %, (alpha 1, beta 0) = 5/10/14/29/43 %, (0, 3) = 82/10/5/1/1, (3, 0) = 0/1/3/22/74. The lesson's predicts l8-trans-1 and l8-trans-2 set both dials the same way.

findings.problem: The rule the dials belong to never appears. Scene 4 teaches 'score = trail times closeness', then scene 6 introduces alpha and beta as 'what the ants trust' with no sign that they are the exponents in trail^alpha x closeness^beta. A learner cannot link the dials back to the scores they just computed, nor see that alpha = beta = 1 is exactly scene 4. The lesson's central formula is p proportional to tau^alpha x eta^beta, and the storyboard comment states it, but nothing on screen does.
findings.fix: Add a small formula tag in the empty band under the dials, for example 'score = trail^α × closeness^β', drawn with L8.tag and SVG signs, popping at 0.9 s with the 'trail' / 'closeness' tags; its α and β take the blue and purple tones. Optionally set the first mode tag to 'α = β = 1: scene 4's rule'.
findings.evidence: Stills s6@2.0 and s6@7.6: dials, 'trail' / 'closeness' tags and bars, no formula. Source comment of scene-06-dials.js states 'trail^alpha x closeness^beta' but no text node does. Lesson l8-transition step 1 'One rule, two ingredients'.

findings.problem: The six-sided die contradicts the number it stands for. A tag reading 'u = random number' sits right beside a die showing 4 pips, while the pointer tag next to the strip says 'u = 0.31'. For draw 2 the die shows 2 pips beside 'u = 0.08'. A first-time learner will ask whether u is 4 or 0.31 (a die cannot give 0.31), and nothing says that u lies between 0 and 1, except the strip's tick labels. The die face is never used by the rule.
findings.fix: Make the die clearly a symbol of chance, not the value: change the tag to 'random draw, 0 to 1' and let the die simply tumble and then fade as the pointer drops (or replace it by a 'spinner' icon). Alternatively show the number on the die face as '0.31'. Do not leave 4 pips next to 'u'.
findings.evidence: Stills s5@3.0 and s5@4.0 (die on 4, 'u = random number', pointer 'u = 0.31') and s5@8.8 (die on 2, 'u = 0.08'). Source: DRAWS[].face = 4 and 2 are arbitrary constants in scene-05-dice.js, unrelated to u.

findings.problem: The scene never says how the ant chooses a job. It shows five grey arrows from Start and then one turns orange, so the pick looks arbitrary, although the lesson says each step is the same transition rule (trail x heuristic, with eta = 100 / due, so a sooner due date is more attractive), and that W is picked first although L is due sooner because the draw is random (W has 47%, L 24%). The scene also lets a learner assume the best schedule is simply built by luck: the heuristic and the pheromone are the whole point of using an ant. Job letters B L P T W also have no meaning on screen (no names, durations or due dates until the chart appears).
findings.fix: Add one tag in the first beat: 'same rule: trail × closeness, sooner due = closer' (or at least 'same choice rule as before'), and a small legend of the five jobs (letter, minutes, due) at 0.5 s, e.g. 'W 50 min · due 30'. Optionally show the first-step shares (B 5%, L 24%, P 19%, T 6%, W 47%) beside the grey arrows.
findings.evidence: Stills s10@2.5 (nodes only), s10@3.6 (five grey arrows, W orange), s10@8.0. Node replay of the lesson's ant (rng 2): step 0 shares B 5 / L 24 / P 19 / T 6 / W 47 %. Lesson l8-schedule steps 'A heuristic: earliest due date' and 'Watch an ant schedule' (quick check 'W is picked first although L is due sooner').

findings.problem: Half of the story the storyboard promises is not shown: 'the ants forget (tabu lists reset), the trails remember (scenes 2-3, lesson 8.1)'. Only the second half is on screen ('The trails are the memory'). Round 2 shows ants standing on new towns with no tabu lists at all, and scene 3 ends with a full tabu row and no sign that it empties for the next tour. Lesson 8.1 has a whole step ('What an ant remembers'), a takeaway and a bank question on exactly this contrast, so a learner can leave thinking the tabu list carries over.
findings.fix: In scene 3's hold (about 11.4-12 s) or scene 2 round 2, clear the tabu row with a short flourish and a tag such as 'new tour: tabu list empty'; or change scene 2's last caption to 'Repeat. Ants forget; the trails remember.' with a tiny empty-list icon on each ant as it pops at 9.2 s.
findings.evidence: Stills s2@9.6 (round 2: ants and thick trails, no tabu lists) and s3@11.5 (tabu list full 'T P Q R S', 'none left'). Outline in lecture-8.json; js/content/nic/l8-01.js step 'What an ant remembers'; js/bank/nic-46.js line 51.

findings.problem: The loop never says when it stops. The outline says the algorithm repeats 'until an end condition' and lesson 8.1 has a 'When to stop' step, but the video ends scene 2 with 'Repeat.' only, and scene 8 just fades after 14 iterations. A first-time learner may think the loop runs forever.
findings.fix: Change caption 4 to "Repeat until done. The trails are the memory." (7 words fit the 11-word limit), and optionally add a small grey "stop?" tag on the loop arrow.
findings.evidence: Caption 4 of scene-02-loop.js; stills s2@9.6, s2@10.9. Lesson step 'When to stop' and takeaway 4 in l8-01.js.

findings.problem: The purple chips in scene 6 show the DISTANCE ('2 km', '10 km'), but purple means closeness, which scene 4 just defined as 1 over the distance and showed as '1/2', '1/4'. With the 'closeness' tag in the same purple, 'beta trusts closeness' sits beside numbers where the biggest is the least close, and a learner must silently invert them.
findings.fix: Either show the closeness values in the chips ('1/2', '1/4', '1/5', '1/8', '1/10') or keep km but label the chips' column 'distance' in grey so the purple 'closeness' tag is not attached to them.
findings.evidence: Still s6@2.0: purple chips '2 km' ... '10 km' under the purple 'closeness' tag; scene-04 chips '1/2', '1/4', '1/5', '1/3'.

findings.problem: Two lesson points are left out. (1) The lateness formula is shown as 'late = ends - due', but the lesson stresses 'or 0 if it finishes early'; here all five jobs are late, so the formula is never tested against an early job. (2) Scene 3 ended with the ant going home; scene 10 never says that a schedule has no way home ('the path is complete when every job is visited', in the storyboard as 'no return').
findings.fix: Make the formula tag 'late = ends - due (never below 0)' if it fits, and add 'no way home' as a small grey tag when the ant reaches B (about 8.9 s).
findings.evidence: Still s10@10.8 (formula 'late = ends - due', all late tags red); lesson l8-schedule steps 'Lateness' and 'The ant's graph'; storyboard scene 10 'the path ends when every job has been used (no way home)'.

findings.problem: Caption 2, 'It picks any town that is still allowed.', reads as a uniform pick. In this very run the lesson's weights are P 40%, Q 11%, R 6%, S 43% for the first step; the video says nothing until scene 4 about the choice being weighted.
findings.fix: Say 'It picks one of the towns that are still allowed.' (weights come next).
findings.evidence: Still s3@3.5 (green options, caption 2); L8.ONE.steps[0].p = 40, 11, 6, 43 (asserted in common.js).

findings.problem: The colony in scene 8 uses alpha 2 and beta 2, but the lesson 8.1 demo ('Run the colony') uses alpha 1 and beta 3 and has only an Ants slider, so a learner who tries the app after the video will not see 'round 2 finds the short loop'. The parameters are not on screen, and the storyboard calls it 'lesson 8.1's ten villages'.
findings.fix: Add a small grey tag 'alpha 2, beta 2, 10 ants' beside 'start' (it fits at 28 px), or say in the page description that the run is a different seed and set-up from the lesson demo.
findings.evidence: common-2.js L8.SNOW = L8.colony(1, {...DEF, alpha: 2, beta: 2}, 14) against l8-01.js DEF = {ants: 10, alpha: 1, beta: 3, rho: 0.5, Q: 100} and colonyDemo controls ['ants']. All SNOW figures were re-derived from the lesson's own iterate() and match.

findings.problem: The recap covers three of the lecture's five lessons. The tabu list, the alpha/beta dials, positive feedback (scene 8), the variants (scene 9) and construction graphs (scene 10) are not recapped, although scenes 8-10 are 38.5 s of the 120.5 s. Row 1's pictogram has three numbered discs but its label names only two steps ('Build tours, then update the trails'); 'place the ants' is not named.
findings.fix: If room allows, change row 1 to "Place, build,\nupdate trails" so all three discs are named, and make row 3 or a spare line mention snowballing or the variants. Otherwise accept: the recap points to Workshop 8.W.
findings.evidence:
Stills s11@6.5 and s11@8.8; scene-11-recap.js rows ['Build tours, then
update the trails', 'Trail times closeness,
then roll the dice', 'Evaporate, then add
Q over tour length'].

findings.problem: Numbers in captions are typed by hand, not read from the asserted helpers, which the house rule asks for. They are all correct today, and asserts nearby pin the data, but captions live in the static caps array and would not follow a data change. Typed: scene 3 'Tour length 74 km', scene 7 'a trail of 4' and 'New trail: 2 + 7 = 9', scene 10 'Average 54 minutes late, worst 70'.
findings.fix: Build the caps arrays from the helpers (for example `Tour length ${L8.ONE.len} km.`, `New trail: ${L8.LEDGER.evap} + ${L8.LEDGER.delta} = ${L8.LEDGER.next}.`, `Average ${L8.SCHED.eval.avg} minutes late, worst ${L8.SCHED.eval.max}.`).
findings.evidence: caps arrays in scene-03-one-ant.js, scene-07-update.js and scene-10-schedule.js. Values verified: 14+13+14+14+19 = 74; (1-0.5) x 4 = 2, 4+2+1 = 7, 2+7 = 9; (20+60+60+60+70)/5 = 54, max 70.
